output.overview: Position the app as a book and document reader: input a document in any format, select a language for text-to-speech pronunciation and voice, then listen to the original content. Language selection does not translate the text.
searchNotes: The product plan incorrectly adds translation. Remove its translator positioning, translated-audiobook promise and foreign-text transformation concept.
Only one supplied reference directly matches the brief. Coverage consists of transcripts and frame descriptions; no video files or attached images were available for inspection.
The supplied frames are indexed segments, not verified openings. Whole-video compliance with the creative constraints is unresolved.
Proposed retrieval phrases: 'import document choose reading voice play' and 'document reader language pronunciation text to speech'.
Unresolved implementation question: How will the requested support for any document format be delivered and verified?
All proposed visuals use original, logo-free interface graphics with no humans, hands or body parts. These are presentation concepts, not evidence of an existing interface.

qualifications.reason: The transcript describes the same core sequence: import a document, choose a reading voice and play. It does not establish this app's format coverage or language-selection behavior.
qualifications.hook: Proposed adaptation: “Your document. Choose a voice. Press play.”
qualifications.title: Listen to documents

qualifications.reason: Its central need is translating a document before listening. That conflicts with the brief's explicit pronunciation-and-voice selector. Shared playback terminology does not make its translation promise transferable.
qualifications.hook: Reject the translation-led hook; do not adapt its language-conversion promise.
qualifications.title: Translate and listen

angles.title: Document to Play
angles.label: Core action sequence
angles.description: Show a document entering the reader, a language being selected for pronunciation and voice, and playback starting.
angles.whyItFits: Makes the stated workflow concrete with minimal explanation. Wanting to listen instead of read is a plausible user situation, not evidence of an additional audience or outcome.
angles.evidence: read-1's transcript says, “Import a document, choose a reading voice and press play.” Its supplied frame description lists a document library and playback controls.
angles.suggestedHook: Your document. Your reading voice. Press play.
angles.visualDirection: Use a proposed, logo-free reader interface with an animated document card, a language selector labeled 'Pronunciation & voice', and a play control. Keep original text unchanged. No humans, hands or body parts.

angles.title: Choose How It Sounds
angles.label: Language-selector clarity
angles.description: Keep a short passage visible while highlighting language selection, then start narration. Explain that the selection controls pronunciation and voice.
angles.whyItFits: Gives the brief's explicit distinction a clear visual treatment without implying translation or adding a separate workflow.
angles.evidence: read-1 explicitly mentions choosing a reading voice before playback. The language-selector meaning comes from the brief; it is not demonstrated by the supplied reference.
angles.suggestedHook: Choose the pronunciation and voice. Hear your original text.
angles.visualDirection: Use logo-free motion graphics: a fixed passage beside a proposed language selector, followed by a playback indicator. Never replace the passage with translated text. No humans, hands or body parts.

storyboard.title: Choose a Voice, Start Listening
storyboard.premise: A 24-second interface-led demonstration of document input, language selection and listening to original content.
storyboard.hook: Turn your document into something you can listen to.

scenes.visual: An unbranded document card moves into a proposed reader interface through graphic animation. On-screen text: 'Bring your document.' No humans or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Bring your book or document, in any format.

scenes.visual: A logo-free language selector opens beside an unchanged passage. Label: 'Language for pronunciation & voice'. No humans or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Select a language for the reading voice and pronunciation.

scenes.visual: The original passage remains fixed. A simple caption reads 'Original text. Selected voice.' All graphics are unbranded; no humans or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Your text stays in its original language. The selection doesn't translate it.

scenes.visual: A play control activates through animation and a playback indicator advances. End card: 'Input. Select. Listen.' Logo-free, with no humans or body parts.
scenes.voiceover: Press play and listen to your content.

storyboard.callToAction: Input a document, select the reading language and press play.
